why: 1-e^{-lambda t} is the cumulative default probability; e^{-lambda t} by itself is the survival probability.
reason: Q = 1 - e^{-lambda t} vs survival e^{-lambda t}; the why is correct.

why: N(d1) is the equity delta that links equity volatility to asset volatility; N(-d2) is the risk-neutral PD. Don't swap d1 and d2.
reason: N(d1) is dE/dV (delta), N(-d2) is the RN PD; correct.

why: EL is linear, EA*PD*LR. UL is EA*sqrt(PD*var_LR + LR^2*var_PD): variances go in, and LR is squared only on the PD-variance term.
reason: Matches both LaTeX strings: variances inside, LR^2 only on var_PD.

why: Same algebra, sqrt(n + n(n-1)rho)/n. In CR-4 it multiplies a loan's UL to get its UL contribution; in CR-19 it is the netting factor on exposure.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Checked algebraically: sqrt(n+n(n-1)rho)/n = sqrt(1/n + rho(1-1/n)). The names and the left-hand sides tell them apart.

why: Both are Euler risk contributions that sum to the total. The UL contribution uses the correlation-weighted UL over UL_P; component VaR uses beta_i*w_i*VaR_p.
reason: Both are Euler contributions; the stated forms match the cards.

why: Both RAROCs net expected losses and tax out of the numerator. The difference is the denominator: credit RAROC divides loan revenues, loan value x (s + f - l - c)(1 - x), by capital at risk (the duration-based change in loan value, -L x D x di/(1+i)). Operational-risk RAROC divides after-tax risk-adjusted net income by economic capital.
reason: Confirmed fix. CR5.tex lines 551-555 define loan revenues = loan value x (s + f - l - c)(1 - x), with l = expected loan losses subtracted, so the original claim of no EL deduction is false. Wording adjusted to show loan value in the revenue term and the Delta L capital-at-risk formula.

why: Sign convention: Hull subtracts a positive CVA and adds DVA (f_nd - CVA + DVA). Gregory writes BCVA = CVA + DVA, with CVA carrying a negative sign.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Checked in the CR-20 source: CVA carries a leading minus sign (Gregory convention); Hull form f_nd - CVA + DVA.

why: The conditional PD has -sqrt(rho)*F. WCDR has +sqrt(rho)*N^{-1}(X) because the worst-case factor is F = -N^{-1}(X).
reason: Sign difference on sqrt(rho) is correct, since the worst-case factor is -N^{-1}(X).

why: The CR-10 capital requirement is the worst-case loss sum(WCDR*EAD*LGD); Basel IRB capital subtracts expected loss, i.e. worst-case minus EL.
reason: CR-10 source (Hull) capital = sum WCDR*EAD*LGD with no EL subtraction; Basel Formula 1 subtracts EL. Correct.

why: 'Firm 1 alone' subtracts the joint probability, pi1 - pi12; 'neither' must add pi12 back, 1 - pi1 - pi2 + pi12.
reason: Inclusion-exclusion is correct.

why: LTV measures collateral coverage (mortgage over appraised value); DTI measures affordability (monthly debt payments over gross monthly income).
reason: Related mortgage-underwriting ratios; correct.

why: The delinquency ratio counts receivables more than 90 days overdue; the default ratio counts receivables already written off.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: The premium leg is weighted by survival probability times spread; the protection leg is weighted by PD times (1 - recovery).
reason: The premium leg uses survival x notional x s and the protection leg uses (1-R) x PD x notional; correct.

why: Loan stressed EL stresses only PD, with EAD fixed; derivative stressed EL stresses both PD and EPE, and EAD = EPE*alpha.
reason: Matches the LaTeX: PD^S only for loans; PD^S and EPE^S*alpha for derivatives.

why: P/L VaR is already in dollars; VaR from return data uses return mu and sigma and must be multiplied by P_{t-1}.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct; the return-based VaR is scaled by P_{t-1}.

why: Normal ES is mu + sigma x phi(z)/(1 - confidence), so tail density over tail probability rather than z; at 97.5% this gives the 2.338 multiplier.
The expected number of exceedances is np (alpha x n), but the historical-simulation VaR is the next observation, (alpha x n) + 1.
reason: Correct; alpha is the tail probability here.

why: LR_uc tests frequency only (chi-square with 1 df, critical value 3.84); LR_cc = LR_uc + LR_ind also tests independence (2 df, critical value 5.99).
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Critical values 3.84 (1 df) and 5.99 (2 df) are correct.

why: Anderson-Darling uses log terms that put extra weight on the tails; Cramer-von Mises weights every squared deviation equally.
reason: AD log terms weight the tails; CvM is unweighted; correct.

why: GEV (block maxima) is exp[-(1 + xi z)^(-1/xi)] with location mu; GPD (peaks over threshold) is 1 - (1 + xi x/beta)^(-1/xi) on excesses over u, with no mu.
reason: Correct; GPD has scale beta and no location mu.

why: Undiversified cash-flow VaR simply adds PV x VaR% (correlation = 1); the ordering principal > duration > diversified refers to the diversified cash-flow VaR.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Consistent with the MR-5-F01 intuition (principal > duration > cash-flow diversified); undiversified uses correlation = 1.

why: Same portfolio variance: the explicit two-asset form needs 2 w_X w_Y cov; the matrix form sqrt(beta_h C beta_v) takes position weights around the covariance matrix.
reason: Correct.

why: F02 gives the change S_t - S_{t-1}; F03 gives the level, so add S_{t-1} back.
reason: Correct.

why: Autocorrelation correlates a series (correlations) with its own one-period lag; the ordinary correlation coefficient relates two different series.
reason: Correct.

why: The DV01-neutral hedge uses the DV01 ratio only; the regression hedge multiplies that same ratio by beta.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: Same structure: F^10 uses DV01^10 and beta^10, while F^30 uses DV01^30 and beta^30. Don't mix up the hedge instrument's DV01.
reason: Correct.

why: The up-state condition uses the up-state discount factor (0.987654) and payoff 0; the down-state condition uses 0.992556 and payoff 2.556.
reason: Checked in the MR-12 source: 0.987654 is the up-state zero price and the up-state payoff is 0; 0.992556 is the down-state price and the payoff is 2.556.

why: The decomposition includes -D dr and the convexity term (1/2)C sigma^2 dt; the expected return for a risk-averse investor is r0 dt + lambda D dt, a duration-based risk premium.
reason: Matches both LaTeX strings.

why: Ho-Lee's drift is an exogenous time-dependent lambda_t; Vasicek's drift k(theta - r) depends on the current rate (mean reversion).
reason: Correct.

why: The tree moves ± sigma sqrt(dt) from r0; the SD of the rate change per step is sigma sqrt(dt), not sigma.
reason: Correct.

why: Ho-Lee is normal (dr has a time-dependent drift); Salomon Brothers is its lognormal counterpart, modeling d[ln r].
reason: Correct: Salomon Brothers is the lognormal analogue of Ho-Lee.

why: Model 3 gets a declining term structure of volatility from sigma e^{-alpha t} with time-dependent drift; Vasicek gets it from mean-reversion k(theta - r) with constant sigma.
reason: Correct per Tuckman: both give declining volatility, by different mechanisms.

why: The lognormal Salomon tree multiplies: r0 e^{a1 dt + sigma sqrt(dt)}. The normal Ho-Lee tree adds: r0 + lambda1 dt + sigma sqrt(dt).
reason: Correct: multiplicative vs additive trees.

why: The Gauss+ short factor r reverts to m with no shock; the medium factor m reverts to l and has correlated shocks rho dW1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) dW2.
reason: Matches the LaTeX: the short factor has no shock term; the medium factor has correlated shocks.

why: Because parity holds for both market and BSM prices, the market-minus-BSM error is the same for a put and a call with the same strike and maturity.
reason: True, and the formulas are visibly different; the error-equality result follows from parity.

why: The default-time copula plugs cumulative default probabilities Q_i(t) into the Gaussian copula in place of generic marginals G_i(u_i).
reason: Correct.

why: Diversified VaR uses sigma_p, which includes correlations below 1; undiversified VaR is just the sum of individual VaRs (rho=1), so it is always greater than or equal to diversified VaR.
reason: Correct.

why: Incremental VaR multiplies MVaR by the new position being added (the change); component VaR multiplies MVaR by the existing holding w_iP, and component VaRs sum to VaR_p.
reason: Checked in the IM-5 source: P_A is the dollar size of the new position. Correct.

why: The global minimum-risk portfolio equalises marginal VaR across assets; the optimal (max risk-adjusted return) portfolio equalises excess return divided by MVaR.
reason: Correct.

why: IR divides alpha relative to a benchmark by tracking error (active risk); SR divides excess over the risk-free rate by total volatility sigma.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: The regression version is ex post: realised excess return R_i - R_F with an alpha intercept. The FF expected-return model is ex ante: E(r_i) = r_f + betas x expected factor premia, with no alpha.
reason: Confirmed fix. The IM3.tex FF box (line 218) has no epsilon, although the CAPM box above it does. The ex post versus ex ante and alpha versus no-alpha distinction matches IM2.tex line 233.

why: The CAPM market premium is average risk aversion times market VARIANCE, gamma*sigma_m^2; active risk aversion is backed out as IR / (2 x active risk sigma_A).
reason: Correct: variance, not standard deviation, in the CAPM premium.

why: For a risky asset m stays inside the expectation with (1+r_i); for the risk-free asset 1+r_f is known, so 1/(1+r_f) = E(m).
reason: Correct.

why: IR_p is just the portfolio's alpha over its active risk, mu_p/omega_p. The manager weight uses IR_p as an input: (IR_i x portfolio TE) / (IR_p x manager TE), which gives more risk to more skilled managers. Don't invert the TE ratio.
reason: Confirmed fix. IM6.tex lines 239-260 give IR_p = mu_p/omega_p and the weight = IR_i x portfolio TE / (IR_p x manager TE). The original why did not name IR_p. The pair is weak, but the fixed line is accurate and separates the two formulas.

why: Jensen's alpha measures return above the CAPM (beta-based) required return; M^2 measures return above the market after matching total risk sigma.
reason: Correct.

why: Allocation = (w_P - w_B) x benchmark return R_B; selection = portfolio weight w_P x (R_P - R_B). Weight difference versus return difference.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: LCR = HQLA / 30-day net cash outflows (short-term survival); NSFR = available stable funding / required stable funding (one-year structural funding).
reason: Correct.

why: Both are VaR plus a liquidation cost. Normal adds sum of s*alpha/2; stressed adds sum of (mu + lambda*sigma)*alpha/2.
reason: Matches the LaTeX.

why: Both widen the spread by a multiple of its volatility. Malz's 99% interval fixes the multiple at 2.33 on the expected (mean) spread s for a single position P, written as a +/- range. Hull's stressed liquidation cost uses mu_i + lambda*sigma_i for a chosen lambda and sums over positions.
reason: Confirmed fix. The LTR2.tex source line is Malz ch. 12, not Dowd, and the vk defines s as the expected (mean) proportional spread. The LTR1.tex source is Hull ch. 24: sum of (mu_i + lambda sigma_i) alpha_i / 2, with lambda = 2.326 at 99%.

why: TSCF+ is built from inflow cfaR+ at quantile alpha; TSCF- is built from outflow cfaR- at 1 - alpha.
reason: Matches the LaTeX.

why: Liquidity gap = change in deposits - change in loans (positive = surplus); AFG = desired loans/investments - expected funds (positive = must borrow). The sign conventions are opposite.
reason: Correct; the signs are opposite.

why: Hot money ratio = money-market ASSETS / volatile LIABILITIES (higher = more liquid, not a total-assets ratio); cash position = (cash + due from banks) / total assets.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: Liquid securities indicator = US govt securities / TOTAL ASSETS (higher = more liquid); pledged securities ratio = pledged / total SECURITIES (higher = LESS liquid).
reason: Correct.

why: Same numerator (expected operating costs). Pooled funds expense divides by ALL new funds; the hurdle rate divides by dollars available for EARNING assets only, so it is higher.
reason: Correct: the same kind of numerator over a smaller denominator gives a higher hurdle.

why: The post-2008 violation says the actual premium EXCEEDS the CIP-implied premium; the basis b is ADDED to the domestic rate r in the numerator to restore equality.
reason: Correct.

why: Change in NII = rate change x CUMULATIVE repricing gap (income view); change in NW uses durations and the discount factor on A and L (market-value view).
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: NIM = (interest income - interest expense) / earning assets, a spread earned; break-even cost rate = (interest + other operating costs) / earning assets, a cost to cover.
reason: Correct.

why: Special spread = GC rate - special rate (positive for specials); that spread, not either rate alone, drives the financing value.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: Plain RAROC is compared with the hurdle rate. Adjusted RAROC first subtracts beta_E x (R_M - R_F) and is then compared with the risk-free rate.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct: ARAROC is compared with R_F.

why: Same beta x (R_M - R_F) term with opposite sign. CAPM ADDS it to R_F to get the cost of equity. ARAROC SUBTRACTS it from RAROC.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: The headline 8% total-capital ratio is the same in both. Basel III adds the 2.5% conservation buffer (10.5%) and tighter Tier 1/CET1 sub-minimums.
reason: Confirmed drop. ORR22.tex (Remember box) says total capital = Tier 1 + Tier 2 = 8% of RWA. ORR21.tex line 46 says total capital / RWA > 8%. These are the same rule. The buffers named in the why are in neither formula, so the pair cannot be split from the formulas.

why: Under Basel I, Tier 1 must be more than 4% of RWA and total capital (Tier 1 + Tier 2) more than 8%.
reason: Confirmed keep (re-checked against the cards and notes): Correct.

why: Both use the multiplier m = 3 + k on average VaR. The ORR formula takes the max with yesterday's VaR and then multiplies by 12.5 to turn capital into market RWA.
reason: Correct: m = 3 + k; 12.5 converts capital to RWA.

why: The Basel II IRB charge uses (DR99.9 - PD) x MA, i.e. unexpected loss only. The credit-reading version multiplies by the full WCDR and subtracts neither PD nor applies MA.
reason: Correct per both source cards (Hull's CR-10 version uses the full WCDR). The wording is slightly awkward but true.

why: BI is the sum of the averaged income components (ILDC + SC + FC). BIC applies the marginal 12%/15%/18% coefficients to BI by bracket, not 18% to the whole of BI.
reason: Correct Basel SA marginal coefficients for bucket 3.
